problems: The square under the well, the seats and the market stall is pale, regular square tiling. It is nearly the same as the Middle Ages and Industrial squares, so the ground carries none of the age change.
Down the column, three of the six ages share the same civic ground.
elements.fix: Bronze square: broad, irregular limestone slabs in mixed sizes (0.8-2 m), slightly rotated, warm sand-limestone colour. Leave wide dusty earth joints (#c9a46a), let packed earth show at the edges with no crisp border, and add a few cracked or missing slabs near the well.

problems: The tall build is captioned 'Sunstep Storehouse Highhouse'. The Stone, Middle and Industrial versions are lodging or living buildings, so in this age the tall-building role turns from homes into storage.
elements.fix: Make it a stepped mudbrick tenement/lodging house: rename it, add doorways at each terrace, ladders, reed awnings and laundry or sleeping mats on the roofs. Drop the storage props (jar stacks, grain bins) as the main read. Keep the stepped silhouette.
